oneliner.t: Mobile businessman and former two-term U.S. representative (2021–2025) who lost the 2024 GOP primary to Barry Moore after redistricting and won the Aug. 11, 2026 Trump-endorsed special primary for the open 1st District.

born.note: Birth date from Wikipedia only; 'Mobile native' confirmed by 1819 News.

upbringing.t: Born in Mobile. Wikipedia lists his high school as Sylacauga High School (1977). He attended Lake City Community College in Florida for a time without a degree, then returned to Mobile to start his first business. He worked at Alabama Power and in sales jobs, founded the health-care equipment company Stat Medical in 1989, later managed at Rotech Medical, and founded Carl and Associates, a management group, in 2003. He married Tina in 1981; they have two children.

education.school: Lake City Community College (now Florida Gateway College)
education.note: Some college, no degree; level kept at hs because no degree was earned.

platform.t: Campaigns on his prior congressional experience and on fighting 'socialist Democrats'; says he will advance Trump's America First agenda.
Earlier campaigns (2020, 2023–24 ads) centered on finishing the border wall and securing the border.
Opposes abortion; called Roe v. Wade 'disastrous' and supported its reversal in 2022.
In 2024 ads pledged to end 'Bidenflation' and expand domestic energy; opposed the 2021 federal oil and gas leasing pause.

promises.t: Bring the Wiregrass 'more opportunities' and better communication from his office (Aug 2025 announcement).
Run a positive campaign without negative ads against rivals (Aug 2025 announcement).

claims.claim: Mobile County Commission president, first elected to the commission in 2012.

said.where: 2020 TV ad / campaign materials as reported by Alabama Daily News

record.t: Served on the Mobile County Commission Nov 2012–Nov 2020; selected president in 2019.

claims.claim: Describes himself as a small businessman.

said.where: 'Told Them' TV ad (2024 cycle), as reported by 1819 News

record.t: Founded Stat Medical (1989) and Carl and Associates (2003), per Wikipedia.

claims.claim: Helped pass legislation funding more border wall construction and more Border Patrol agents.

said.where: 'Told Them' TV ad (2024 cycle), as reported by 1819 News

record.t: Carl voted Yea on H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act of 2023, which passed the House 219–213 on May 11, 2023 (Roll Call 209). The bill provided for building a border wall, but the Senate never acted on it and it did not become law. So he helped pass it in the House only. The Border Patrol agent increase was not confirmed against the bill text, since Congress.gov and GovInfo could not be opened. (Rating changed from unverifiable to partly in the Oct 8, 2026 pass.)

claims.claim: Trump has endorsed him 'twice already in two other races.'

said.where: 2026 campaign announcement, as reported by 1819 News

record.t: No primary record of the 2020/2022 endorsements was opened. Trump's 2026 endorsement is documented by the Alabama Reflector. The Wikipedia pages for Alabama's 2020, 2022 and 2024 House elections list no Trump endorsement of Carl; the 2024 page lists Trump endorsements for other Alabama Republicans but not for Carl. Those lists are not complete, so this is not proof the endorsements did not happen, and the rating stays unverifiable.

claims.claim: Building his name recognition cost $1.3 million.

said.where: FM Talk 106.5 radio interview, as reported by 1819 News

record.t: FEC shows his committee spent $2.23M in 2019–20, $0.97M in 2021–22, $2.63M in 2023–24 and $0.87M in 2025–July 2026. No breakdown supports or refutes the $1.3M figure.

claims.claim: Says the name recognition he has built rests on efforts over the last 15 years.

said.where: FM Talk 106.5 radio interview, as reported by 1819 News

record.t: He was first elected to the Mobile County Commission in 2012, served as its president from 2019, and was in the U.S. House from 2021 to 2025. That is about 14 years in elected office by 2026, so the round figure is about right.

claims.claim: Says he has built several healthcare businesses.

said.where: 2020 campaign website, Issues page (healthcare), as preserved on Ballotpedia; the current site could not be opened

record.t: Wikipedia names one healthcare company he founded (Stat Medical, a health-care equipment firm, 1989) and a management job at Rotech Medical. That section of Wikipedia carries no citation, and no business-registration records were checked.

claims.claim: Describes himself as an avid hunter and a lifetime NRA member.

said.where: 2020 campaign website, Issues page (Second Amendment), as preserved on Ballotpedia

record.t: NRA membership records are not public. Wikipedia records NRA Political Victory Fund endorsements and grades (2020, 2022), but these do not show membership.

entries.t: Opposed the American Rescue Plan as too big and rushed.
Voted for the Fiscal Responsibility Act (debt-ceiling deal).
Voted to sustain the objections to Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes.
Said he was not bothered by McCarthy's Jan. 6 remarks and that he had said things that day he regretted.
Declined Clyde Jones's general-election debate challenge; said a debate is 'totally out of the question.'

aipac_endorse.t: Not checked — AIPAC's endorsement page is not on this environment's allowed source list.

aipac_pac.note: Not listed on Track AIPAC's Congress or Candidates pages (he is a former member/2026 candidate); career total not available from that source.

statements.t: As congressman-elect, said 'We will stand very firm with Israel.'
Called Israel 'America's most important regional ally' (Yellowhammer News, per Wikipedia).
Voted for Israel-support legislation after the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack (per Wikipedia).

fec.src_note: pac_all = 'other committee contributions' from the FEC summary; the business vs. ideological split was not available (itemized Schedule A not reachable). 'other' = $183,453.86 transfers from his joint fundraising committee (Jerry Carl Victory Committee) + $2,000 offsets.
fec.quarters_note: Rounded figures from Alabama Daily News reporting of FEC filings ('more than'/'about').
fec.outside_note: No outside spending for or against Carl in 2026 was found in news coverage; FEC outside-spending tables did not load. In the 2024 primary he lost, House Freedom Action spent $759,000 against him and Club for Growth's School Freedom Fund spent $581,000 for Moore; South Alabama Conservatives PAC ran ~$50,000/week of TV against Moore (Ballotpedia).

history.note: Refunded $277,999 in contributions; repaid $176,202.71 of candidate loans. Coverage dates not shown on the page (two-year period 2023–24).

fec.history_note: Candidate loans in 2020 were $758,900; FEC shows candidate-loan repayments of $325,900 (2019–20), $28,797.29 (2021–22) and $176,202.71 (2023–24), totalling $530,900. Debts owed by the committee are still $254,535.87; the page does not itemize them. He also sponsors two leadership PACs named Conservative American Republican Leadership PAC (C00752287, C00919506), whose finances were not pulled.

corp.t: Business PACs: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alabama and the Alabama Farmers Federation gave in Q4 2025 (Alabama Daily News). PAC/committee money was $387,000 (2020), $499,500 (2022), $634,500 (2024) and $303,059 (2025–Jul 2026), but FEC summaries do not split it into business and ideological PACs.

money2.note: Sen. Katie Britt's leadership PAC gave $10,000 (June 2026); Rep. Dale Strong and the House GOP leadership campaign committee also gave (ADN, Jul 22, 2026). Itemized top-donor lists were not reachable.

trades.note: MarketBeat reports 'No trade activity.' House periodic transaction reports were not checked directly.

note.t: House financial disclosures (disclosures-clerk.house.gov) use a search form this tool cannot submit, so his annual reports and net worth were not reviewed.

effectiveness.note: Sponsored/enacted counts not taken: congress.gov and GovTrack are blocked. A third-party profile (The Lobby) lists 10 sponsored bills (3 in the 117th, 7 in the 118th), all at 'introduced' status, but its completeness is unverified.

democracy.t: Voted Yea on the objection to Arizona's electoral votes (Roll Call 10; failed 121–303).
Voted Yea on the objection to Pennsylvania's electoral votes (Roll Call 11; failed 138–282).
On Mobile radio, said he had no problem with McCarthy's leaked Jan. 6 remarks and admitted saying things that day he had to 'ask God to forgive me for.'

note.t: Mobile native and Mobile resident; Mobile County is in AL-01 under the 2023 map. Exact years of residence are not documented (he attended high school in Sylacauga and college in Florida before returning to Mobile).

research_notes: Coverage: FEC candidate pages for 2020, 2024 and 2026 and the committee page for 2022 were read directly (the 2022 candidate page hit a rate limit). Carl's 2026 summary runs through July 22, 2026 (pre-special-primary report). ADN's July 22 article said no debts were reported; the FEC summary shows $254,535.87 in debts owed by the committee, unchanged since 2024, and carried over from his 2020 candidate loans. A Gateway Pundit item (Mar 2026) quoted him calling Trump a 'lame duck' and doubting a Trump endorsement; that source is strongly partisan and not used for findings. Trump did endorse him before the Aug. 11 special primary (Alabama Reflector). Endorsements also reported: Sen. Katie Britt, Speaker Mike Johnson, Rep. Jim Jordan (1819 News). Special-primary result: 74.7% (23,325 of 31,225 votes, unofficial, NBC 15). He declined all debates with Democrat Clyde Jones. The web-search budget ran out partway through, so some lines of inquiry (lawsuits, 2026 ads) were not searched further. [Oct 8, 2026 claims/checklist pass] CLAIMS: the mechanical sample still could not be run because the current campaign site is unreachable. Campaign site unreachable again this pass: direct fetches were refused (the proxy blocked the domain, and the fetch tool only opens URLs that have already turned up in a search or fetch result), web.archive.org was blocked, and the shared web-search budget was used up before any new search could run. So the work was limited to pages already cited in this file or linked from them. I re-rated the border-wall ad claim as partly after checking Roll Call 209 (H.R. 2 passed the House with his Yea vote, but never became law). I added three claims: one true and two unverifiable from his 2020 site as preserved by Ballotpedia. The checkable-verdict count is 4 of the 5 required, so checklist.claims stays "news". The re-check of 1819 News coverage found no factual claims about votes, bills or money in his Aug 2025 announcement. DISCLOSURES: still "no". disclosures-clerk.house.gov search URLs and PDFs could not be opened, because no PDF link could be surfaced without search. ETHICS: "news" (Wikipedia/The Lobby show nothing; OCE/House Ethics were not opened). DEMOCRACY: unchanged ("done"). Ballotpedia notes House Freedom Action spent $759,000 opposing him in the 2024 primary (context only).
